utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Turkalj. I would like it remind you -- I would like to remind that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony, that is, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I have document P606, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, you compiled a record referred to as the war path or the war record for the Lucko Unit on the orders of Mr. Markac, did you not? And you'll see the document in a moment on the screen. This was compiled by you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: It was drafted by my unit colleagues, and I signed the report. I am familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What were the sources of information for the report? And I -- we will go through -- this is just a cover note. What were the sources of information based on which this report was compiled and submitted?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The entire report was drafted, based on the knowledge an information that was in possession of some of the employees that were in the field, and the data from various log-books and rosters of those who were in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And it's -- the cover note indicates that it's -- it was submitted on 16 February 1998. To whom did you submit this report to?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This report was submitted to the special police sector, to the chief personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Who had access to this report, apart from the chief? For example, did the inner control branch have access, did Mr. Markac have access to this report?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely who had access to it. It was forwarded to the special police sector, and the chief at the time was Mr. Sacic. As for who had access to it and what he did with the report is something I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you turn to the Croatian version, page 91, and in the English page 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, I'll take you to the section for -- which is -- which reports on the operation on 25th and 26th August. Now, when was this section compiled? Is it in 1998, since you submitted the report in 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the operation on the 25th, this report has no reference to people being killed and houses burning in the course of the operation. Did anybody, either Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic or the inner control branch, question you about the absence of that -- such information with regard to that particular operation in this report?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This report on the war path did not contain such information. It mainly focussed itself on what the tasks of the unit were, starting with 1990 until the end of 1995. In such reports, such war paths, one does not include that type of information. It only contains information on the whereabouts of the unit at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So what was the basis or what was the source of information based on which you reported for the 25th August operation in this record? What were your other -- the underlying reports that you used?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As regards this report, we used solely the orders we had received for particular tasks. It was based on the commands orders that is, and on the participation of individual people included in those tasks. No additional information was provided in the war path, and you could probably see the same pattern when other operations in the course of that period are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in this report there is no reference to an operation being conducted on the 26th of August. You were aware that there was an operation conducted in the area of the Promina hills on the 26th August, were you not? You have, in fact, referred to in your interview transcripts. Why is that not referred to?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: That is correct. However, in this report, among all the other reports that have to do with Operation Storm, this one, all -- includes the 25th and 26th of August as well -- with regards to Operation Oluja-encirclement. It was a single operation. I don't know whether you get my point. Reports were not drafted on the particular details of any given operation. This is merely a report on the war path of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's correct. But the point is you just told Court, Mr. Turkalj, that what you recorded here as to where the units were at a particular time. Now you are aware there was operation on 25th, and you were aware that there was another operation on the 26th in another area, in the -- in the area of the Promina hills. So why is that not referred to in this report? That's my question to you.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The employees drafting this report probably did not find it necessary to include any details. That's why they use the term Operation Storm encirclement, including both the 25th and 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: To repeat, this is not a report on the specific tasks. This mainly concerns the name of the operation and the whereabouts of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well. I will move on. Can I just ask you, Mr. Turkalj, to turn to your transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, if I could have your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is P1152, that is section three of -- the ERN number is V000-5305. If I could ask you, Madam Usher, to turn to page 49.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Turkalj, before we go into that, are you aware of any reports relating to the 26th August operation in the Promina hills existing within the Lucko Unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I think this is 1152.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, it came up as 1162.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It should be 1152, but I believe I said 1152.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, if you could answer me, are you aware -- Mr. Turkalj are you aware of reports -- before you go through that, Mr. Turkalj, can you answer my question. Are you aware of reports relating to the 26th August operation in the Promina hills existing within the Lucko Unit?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to see such reports at that time. I did see some later, however. To repeat, the reports were not sent to the unit itself but to the command of operations. That is a different thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you said you saw reports later, when did you see reports relating to the 26th August operation later? When was that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: When I received such documents from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: From who -- Mr. Turkalj, we did not show you any documents relating to the 26th August operation. What are you -- I'm not relating to the Grubori event. I'm relating to the operation in -- on the 26th in the Promina hills. Have you ever seen any reports, written reports, related to that operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I don't recall such reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in -- on page 49 you refer to this operation. And you refer to what Mr. Celic told you about that operation, and this is what you say: "I can say only what I talked about with Celic and what he told me in that aspect. He told me that they had a search in that area, that you mentioned, although I still do not know which particular part they were searching. He told me - next page - that some houses were set on fire during the search. And he told me that Mr. Markac talked to him and to some other people from the unit, more specifically one instructor whose name is Franjo Drljo. That is, once again, I learned from Celic because I was not present there." Then the last -- "Celic also mentioned that it was not a pleasant conversation and that Drljo said to Markac words to the effect, So I did it, so I burned them, so what now? Kill me if you want." And you go on up from that point onwards, Mr. Turkalj, you go on to describe what Mr. Celic told you and which -- that was a conversation that took place between Mr. Markac and Mr. -- Mr. Markac and Franjo Drljo where Drljo told him that he had burned houses. Now, apart from that, did Mr. Celic tell you any further details about that operation of the 26th?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No, there was no further discussion about the operation. At the beginning of my testimony, I said that subsequently I talked to Mr. Janjic who said that he had investigated that event.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you were informed by your assistant commander Celic that Mr. Drljo had admitted to the commander of the special police, Mr. Markac, that he had burned houses. Now, what did you as commander of the Lucko Unit do about that? Why didn't you take any measures against Drljo?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Regarding that, I cannot state precisely that Celic told me of someone who had confirmed to him that they had burned houses. In any case, Celic told me there was fighting and firing and some houses were set ablaze but not in the sense that it was arson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to this line of questioning, we had a witness, Mr. Celic, who came here to testify. He was asked nothing about these issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is an inappropriate intervention while the witness is listening to this. May I just ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we ask the witness to take his earphones off. Ms. Mahindaratne, could you please respond to --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if Mr. Kuzmanovic would read Mr. Celic's transcripts which are all in evidence, Mr. Kuzmanovic will see Mr. Celic's testimony about 26th August operation, which is exactly what is stated here by this witness. Mr. Celic talks about the conversation between Mr. Markac and Mr. -- and Drljo where Drljo admits to burning of houses. I think Mr. Kuzmanovic should read the transcripts first before rising to his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I totally disagree with that assertion, and Mr. Celic was here, and these questions should have been asked of him directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, well, if it is part of a written statement which is admitted into evidence, then, of course, there's no -- Ms. Mahindaratne, could you give us the page references for Mr. Celic's --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, can I do it after the break because I don't have the page in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, otherwise I will try to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My position, Your Honour, is if this is just another part of another document that she's referring to that we received when we have 92 ter statements and materials for witnesses, that's one thing. He was here on the stand; he could have asked the questions directly. He wasn't. Now they're trying to go through a witness, basically a double hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. If it is in his 92 ter statement, and I'll check that immediately - I can't tell that you I have a lot on my mind - then it is entirely appropriate what Ms. Mahindaratne does. Ms. Mahindaratne, if you, meanwhile, proceed, then I'll try to find the relevant ... Could the witness ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Turkalj, you just said that Mr. Celic told you that there had been combat activity. Now, how is it that you have never mentioned that either in your statement or the interview? The statement during -- can you not hear me or ... Mr. Celic [sic], your evidence was I cannot state precisely that Celic told me. You said: "Celic told me Mr. Was fighting and firing and some houses were set ablaze but not in the sense that it was arson." Now how come you never mentioned either in your statement of 2004 or at the interview there 2005 that Celic told you that there was firing and the houses were burned in the course of the combat activity? You never mentioned that. Why are you saying that for the first time here?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I must confess it was very difficult to remember every word after so many years, and it all depended on the investigator's questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. I move on. Mr. Turkalj -- but let me just ask one question. Did you have ever question Franjo Drljo about this conversation between him and Mr. Markac, or did you find out what really happened in the course of that conversation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No. As regards that part, I did not talk to Mr. Drljo, given that the operation commander had inquired into the event, and Drljo must have explained that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Markac ever call you up, or did Mr. Sacic ask you to call up any reports regarding the 26th August operation either from Celic or any other special instructors involved in that operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to continue to object to this line of questioning. She's not listening. I'd ask the witness to take off the headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please take off your earphones for a while, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. He has already answered two or three times that the commander of the operation was the one who investigated this incident. And she keeps asking him whether he did so, and he keeps saying the same thing. The commander of this operation investigated this incident. I don't know we need to go any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I do. I think it's because Mr. Kuzmanovic was not listening to my question, Mr. President. My question was did Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic ever ask this witness to call up reports from the -- from -- his assistant commander Celic or any other special instructors to written reports on this operation, as Mr. Markac had then done with regard to 25th August operation. I think Mr. Kuzmanovic has a difficulty in, you know, differentiating between these questions. These are frivolous objections to say the least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You know what, Counsel, I would really prefer that we not get into those sort of language issues. This is an issue with respect to your methodology of questioning. This witness has answered the question on more than one occasion, and I'm sure he will answer it the same way again if he gets asked, so if you want to continue to waste time, that's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's only Monday morning, and now already -- I'm just checking. I'm trying to check a lot of things at the same time. Last question by Ms. Mahindaratne was, whether this witness was ever called upon to produce a report. Whether he investigated himself is a different matter. So to that extent, the objection is denied. And could you refrain from unnecessary interruptions. Ms. Mahindaratne, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, let me repeat my question to you. Were you ever asked by Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic to call reports from Celic -- Josip Celic or any other special instructors to submit written reports on the operation on the 26th as he did with regard to the operation on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No. There was no such a request.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me take you, Mr. Turkalj, and this is my last line of questions. If I could ask you to turn to page 126 on the same section. That is P1152. That's V000-5305, page 126. Now your testimony was that at some stage the deputy commander of the Lucko Unit, Mr. Curkovic - pardon my pronunciation - informed you, told you, that one of the members of the Lucko Unit, namely Igor Beneta may have participated in the incident on 25th August in Grubori. It's at page 126 and 127. Now, did you ever ask him what the basis of that information was?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This was only in an informal conversation that I heard the name, but it could not be absolutely checked up on, nor could direct knowledge be obtained in relation to anything. I can't really confirm anything in relation to this particular conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When were you told that by Mr. Curkovic?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I can't recall that either. I can't pinpoint the time. At any rate, it was at a certain point in time after the action.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you three documents --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't certain of the last witness's last answer. Could he please repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, could you please repeat your answer again. Mr. Turkalj, could you say what you said earlier on, your answer, repeat your answer, with regard to the time-frame when he may have told you this.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I said that it wasn't shortly after the action. It could have been several years later. I can't recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, I'm going to show you three documents, and I'll ask you a couple of questions about them. I'll just show you those documents, and you ought to be familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could I have document 6447, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You will see in a moment, Mr. Turkalj, on the screen a report sent by you to the special police sector regarding the matter of transfer of Igor Beneta and others dated 21st October, 1995. This is your document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Why was Mr. -- whose proposal was it to transfer Mr. Igor Beneta in this stage, something like one month from the incident in Grubori? Whose proposal was it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This was solely on the proposal from the unit. But it had nothing to do with those events. This was regular procedure of transferring members to new posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Was there a regular procedure when members were transferred from the unit? Was there a roster, or how was it done?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: There was no specific or concrete procedure in place. It depended on the requests coming from individual members. Somebody wanted to take a different post or be dispatched to a different town or village. For the most part, it was the result of an agreement between the commander and the individual, or in regard to some members, there was such a working relationship where the superiors felt that it was better for these individuals to be transferred to some other posts. This was nothing unusual.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So generally these transfers took place on the basis of a request from the individual concerned or in consultation with the individual concerned, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: That's correct too. What's also correct is that there was a request from the command where we would be possibly asking for their transfer to a new post. Let me repeat, I don't see anything unusual in the document. This was regular procedure, not only applied by this unit but by all units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And can the individual concerned in the course of this type of regular procedures, as you say, do the individuals concerned resist such transfers, or do they refuse to accept the transfer or ...

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The ministry worked in such a way, and I mean the Ministry of Interior, that every member of the ministry can be transferred or granted transfer to another post. Of course, this decision can be complained against, a complaint can be lodged against it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if a complaint is lodged against such a decision is there a procedure involved where it is reconsidered, or is there an inquiry? What is generally done?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This isn't a matter for us. It is it a matter for the personal service.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question is, Mr. Turkalj, and I will be very specific. For instance, when a decision to transfer a member of the Lucko Unit is made, can the -- that member refuse to accept the transfer paper, resist it quite -- let us say, refuse to accept the papers, just, you know, resist it in such a way, not go through regular procedure of moving for an appeal against such a decision?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The transfer decision is serviced upon an individual by the personnel service and only by the personnel service, not by the commander. Everyone who receives such a decision is allowed to appeal the decision within, I believe, six or seven days, and this is the practice that still exists today. And the appeal or complaint is filed with the personnel service.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did Mr. Sacic, as the chief of the sector, get involved in these transfer procedures, either proposing that a transfer be made, or that if a member resists a transfer in cancelling that previous decision; or is it only the personnel department that gets involved in such procedures?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I don't think that it was within the competence of Mr. Sacic to do that. That was within the purview of the personnel service. When we're talking about the level of the units themselves, they produce proposals; they don't issue decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P1157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1157 is admitted into evidence. Ms. Mahindaratne, on Friday you told us you would need another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I checked with Mr. Registrar. He said that looking very carefully at the time taken and interruptions et cetera that you had had approximately 30 minutes, but you've taken this 30 minutes already. Could you please wrap up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I will just tender two documents and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I have document 6448, please. Mr. President, let me just tender those two documents in the bar table, so I had not waste any time. Document number 6448 and 6449, I will tender from the bar table. I don't have to have any questions from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- you know the procedure for bar table documents, is that you briefly describe them and that you -- now these are relatively short ones, and apparently they are follow-ups in relation to the last one, is that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there, although the formality is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't object to this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You wouldn't object, and since I do not hear any objections from the other Defence teams, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 6448 becomes exhibit number P1158. And 65 ter 6449 becomes exhibit number P1159.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1158 and P1159 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, we handed over to you during the first break on Friday, the -- an interview -- a record of an interview that Ministry of Interior officials had had with you, and you were asked to review that document and let us know if there were any mistakes or if the record was an accurate reflection of the interview. Do you have anything to say about that note? If perhaps on the screen, Mr. Registrar, if could I have 2537; that is the document. Do you recall the note that was given to you, Mr. Turkalj?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Is that an accurate reflection of the interview that was conducted by the Ministry of Interior officials with you in 2004?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: It is not an accurate reflection of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are there many mistakes?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The contents in their entirety are different from what we talked about, and from the statement I gave to the ICTY investigators. In the last sentence, it is even stated that the statement is identical to the one given to the ICTY investigators. In fact, it is not. Besides, this is an Official Note, not a statement, which I didn't either see or sign.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not tender that, Mr. President. That concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne. Mr. Mikulicic, I got a estimate of the time you would need. Could I receive from other counsel an estimate as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may be one session, or I may not be any questions at all. We're reviewing the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will be very brief, half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half an hour. Then, Mr. Mikulicic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Since we will be speaking in the same language, for technical reasons, namely interpretation, I kindly ask you to be mindful of the fact that we have to make a break between questions an answer, so please make a short pause after you have heard my question before answering so that the interpreters can do their job. Mr. Turkalj, in the line of questions the Prosecutor just put to you, there was reference of the arson -- or, rather, the firing of houses on 26th of September -- of August, 26th of August, 1995, which was conducted by the anti-terrorist unit Lucko. Though you were a commander of the unit, you were not out on the field on that day, were you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The operational commander in the field was Mr. Celic; was he not?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The commander of the overall action was Mr. Janjic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You were asked about whether you spoke to anyone in the wake of the action, and you said that you spoke both to Mr. Celic and Mr. Janjic. We heard the testimonies of both of these individuals in court. Can you please clarify one portion of the statement by Mr. Janjic who said here in his testimony that Mr. Markac had personally tasked him with investigating the circumstances which led to the houses being set on fire and he assumed -- and he said that he assumed that task upon himself. What did Mr. Janjic tell you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I believe that I mentioned my conversation with Mr. Janic, and he said that he had met with Mr. Markac who had tasked him with inquiring into the matter. That's to say the events in which the unit was involved on -- of, in, on the 26th. Mr. Janjic told me that he had, in fact, inquired and reported to Mr. Markac about what had happened in the area on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic stated in this courtroom that he claimed that the houses came to be set on fire due to the fact that a rocket launcher had been fired at them. What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: He told me that after they had investigated the matter he had information to the effect that there was fighting going on and that, in fact, the houses came to be -- or were set on fire, through the firing of a rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There was another incident which is the subject of this case which we heard a lot of evidence about that. That's in the Plavno valley, specifically in the village of Grubori. This Chamber heard that the event took place on the 25th of August, while a mop-up operation was going on, one in which your anti-terrorist unit Lucko took place. You were not out in the field at that time either, were you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The information you have about the event are, in fact -- is, in fact, indirect information you received from those who took part in what happened. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Following these events and following your visit, personal visit, to the village of Grubori which you testified about last week, you said that it -- it was your impression that there was some fighting going on there. You were sent by the commander of the special police to ask from the commander of the action Mr. Celic and the instructors to submit their reports, which is what you did. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. And I said as much last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When the written reports were being written, was any sort of duress, measures of coercion applied towards Mr. Celic and the instructors to draft the reports this way or the other, or was it entirely left up to them to write the reports as they wished?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: All the members of the unit had their rooms on the premises of the unit, and once I gave them the order to produce the report, they produced the reports independently, and nobody told them in any way how to write the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The leaders of the group that were formed in the action of the search operation, and they were asked to produce the report. We know that Mr. Drljo did not produce a report. However, is it true that Mr. Drljo verbally reported to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I reported to Mr. Markac about the fact that Mr. Drljo did not produce a written report. Mr. Drljo, on his part, told me that he had not been there. That he was not aware of what took place in Grubori, that he had only heard gunshots and that he believed as a result of that, he need not write a report. It was on the basis of this information that I reported to Mr. Markac accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Drljo tell you that he would not be submitting a report in addition to other matters also because he was not a group leader?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. He said something to that effect. This was an insult to him, since he was an instructor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the registrar please call up 65 ter 3258.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And can the counsel and the witness make a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both you, Mr. Mikulicic, and you, Mr. Turkalj, are invited to make a break between question and answer, and then answer and question. Ms. Mahindaratne, if meanwhile, if could you try to find the relevant portion of the Celic statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I did, Mr. President, but I just wanted to, for what it's worth, just check -- in fact, my colleague did check, and have I got the transcript reference numbers where it was discussed in court as well as the -- in the statement, the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be a good idea if you just sent by e-mail the relevant page numbers so that everyone can check, and if you would please then copy the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The Chamber. Yes I will do that. I will do that at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it is not evidence; it is just assisting us in finding the relevant portions you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkalj, on our screens we can see the report from the criminal investigation police department sent to the county state attorney's office or state attorney in Sibenik on the issue of what happened in Grubori, and it dates from 2004. Do you agree with me that -- this points to a conclusion that back in 2004, still an investigation was ongoing about the events that transpired in Grubori nine years previously?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. I have not seen this report before, but since it was sent by the criminal investigation police to the state attorney's office, or to the state attorney, evidently there was an investigation under way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would like to direct you to paragraph 2 of the report, where the CID informed the state attorney as follows: "However, as is evident from these interviews," and they're referring to the interviews conducted in paragraph 1 of this report, "we still have not been able to establish the compositions of the groups and the possible commanders of these groups. The reason being that all the above-mentioned members of the anti-terrorist unit stated that there had been no strict division into groups during the operation but that they had acted jointly on the ground, and that then, depending on the lie of the land, and internal friendships between individuals, they moved on, either in small groups or in pairs." Mr. Turkalj, this sort of an interpretation of the lie of the land and the type of the land which is mountainous and forested, is it consistent with what you know of this search operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no objection. This was a document included in the bar table submission with regard to this witness. So maybe Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there is no need you would say -- the bar table you just --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Registrar, if you would ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that, at this moment, only one document is then tendered. Mr. Registrar will verify, and you can also verify whether Chamber can -- at this moment whether the other document is the same as the one tendered by Ms. Mahindaratne, if so, we leave it as it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I just also say that that bar table submission was not copied to the -- to the Chambers yet because we are awaiting objections from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean bar table submission and not the two bar table documents you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You said one of the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Trying to find out what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, if that is the case, then I would say that we strike from bar table submissions whatever is tendered into evidence and admitted into evidence by the other party before the bar table procedure has been completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Registrar, the ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D1200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1200 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you strike it from your bar table submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll do that, Mr. President. I'm doing that right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkalj, while we can still this document on the screen which you say indicates that nine years after the Grubori incident, an investigation was still pending about it, do you have any sort of information today about the fact that in the village of Grubori, on the 25th of August, 1995, a crime would have been committed, and do you have information about who would have been the one for whom there would have been reasonable suspicion that the individual had committed the crime?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I don't have any specific information about there having been committed a crime or about the possible perpetrator thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In other words, if you don't have that sort of information today, you did not have it back then; in other words, in the months of August or September 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No, we did not have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the situation when Mr. Drljo did not wish to submit a written report, did you have any indications that he might have been connected with the crimes in the village of Grubori and that was why he did not wish to submit a written report perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No. Absolutely there were no indications of Mr. Drljo participating in any such event that could have been tied in with the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You told us, Mr. Turkalj, that Mr. Drljo was an undisciplined member of the special police unit, mildly speaking, but, on the other hand, that he was a very good fighter. Was it your assessment when he was not punished because he did not write the report, you as the commander had all of these conditions in mind?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Well, all I can say is that Mr. Drljo did not respect authority simply as a person. That was one of his character traits. But, on the other hand, I can confirm that he was an excellent fighter, since we were in the middle of war. He did have authority in the unit and broader when fighting was concerned, so I believe that one report was not a reason to submit a request for disciplinary measures. At that point in time, for me, I won't say that it was an unimportant, but let's say that it was not important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, when you were at the scene of the crimes together with Mr. Sacic, Balunovic in Grubori, and you saw that there were many people there according to what you said, and they included some members of the police, of the local police station, were you able to notice if the local police was informed about the events in the village of Grubori?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: In my testimony, I said that there were many people there. I think -- or I thought that there were some members of the regular police there, and that made it clear that they were informed about the events in the same way as those who had just arrived to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Since you are a person who participated in the events, I would like to ask about your reaction. It is indisputable that in the police there was a criminal police section, which was in charge of looking for perpetrators of crimes and evidence.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Within the police in control of that area and the general city police who were there, they only dealt with criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's correct, isn't it, Mr. Turkalj, that special police did not have a section for crime, did not investigate criminal acts, or look for perpetrators of crimes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: However, on the other hand, if the criminal police actions or the judicial organs were to establish that some member of the special police did commit a specific crime and if the special police command was informed of that, measures would then be taken, wouldn't they? Certain disciplinary measures?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Well, I would like to correct you a little bit. If we're talking about crimes, specifically if it's a crime, we're not taking disciplinary measures, then we're talking about an investigation, and then I, as the commander, could then provide the opportunity to interview the member the police were interested in, and we could provide some logistic support, if this was being asked of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the registrar to show us D1078, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, you will see on your screen shortly a decision under which a member of the anti-terrorist Lucko, Mario Spekuljuk, was relieved of duty because criminal proceedings were initiated against him in the investigation centre of the county court in Zagreb, and that's where he was also detained. So we see a situation here when possible perpetrator of a crime was identified, and on that basis, you will see on the following page, Mr. Markac, made a decision to suspend him from duty. Is this a procedure that you are familiar with and that was usual for cases like that, when a member of the anti-terrorist unit that you were heading had committed a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: You can see from this document that investigations were initiated against Mr. Spekuljuk and that Mr. Markac, therefore, suspended him from duty pursuant to the relevant rules of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move to another topic; that is, the topic of the procedure of repair and write-off of weapons in the anti-terrorist unit, Lucko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry please show us document 3D01-0702.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for the document to appear, it's correct, isn't it, Mr. Turkalj, that the procedure to repair, inspect and write-off weapons was regulated in writing at the Ministry of the Interior. There were documents about that, and here we see the rules of procedure, with official personal, arms, weapons and ammunition which was adopted by the minister of the interior. Mr. Turkalj, did you have the opportunity to familiarize yourself with these rules?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The rules were in force, and we operated on the basis of its regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at Article 6 of the rules in the Croatian text. This is on page 3, which states: "A police administration structural unit, authorised for matters of operational technical equipment, conducts periodical inspections and maintenance of personal arms in a police administration." Simply stated, are we talking about the weapons maintenance plant here?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: We're talking about the structural unit of the police administration, and it has to do with the repair of technical equipment of the police administration, and you can say that we're talking about the weaponry repair and maintenance workshop. It's part of that section.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Article 6, paragraph 2 says that: "The structural unit ... in accordance with its own inspection plan at least once a year, conducts inspections of the complete personal arsenal ..." Is this something that concords with the practice in the anti-terrorist unit Lucko, as well as in all the special police units, as well as in the general police units?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I have already said that that was the usual procedure, and we can conclude on the basis of these rules that each year, an inspection was carried out of weapons and equipment as well as the operation of the depots, and the procedure was something that applied to all our operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If it were to be established that certain weapons that were inspected were found to be faulty, they would be repaired, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The commission that inspected the weapons would decide whether the weapons -- whether it was possible to repair the weapons or not, depending on the state they were in, and then depending on their assessment if it was possible to repair the weapons, they would be sent to the workshop, repaired and returned to the unit. If it was not possible to repair the weapons, that -- to the extent that it was not worth repairing the particular piece, it would be written off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to Article 9 of this document. This is on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Article 9 talks about the procedure of writing off personal equipment, and we're talking about what you just mentioned, that in case it was not possible to repair the weapons, or it would not be worthwhile this repair them, a report would be compiled, and they would be proposed for write-off. So this was a regular procedure, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly what I said a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1201 is admitted into evidence. Although, Mr. Mikulicic, it appears to be a provisional translation, very informal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... The official translation has -- yes, has been requested, and we will have it in due course. That's what was our information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the -- the official translation will then replace the provisional translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can we now please look at document 6165, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The document that we just looked at were the rules on handling weapons drafted or adopted by the minister, and the implementation of the rules actually is a kind of instruction about how to write-off weapons. Can we now look at this document, on page 2. So these instructions were adopted on the basis of the rules that we just looked at, and it was adopted by the chief of the weaponry special equipment and technical protection. Can we look at the next page with text, please. We could say that this is an operative document which specifies how to handle weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. It's a guideline, it means that it provides an explanation how -- of how to write-off weapons. That procedure is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And now we can see in paragraph 2 that a commission is formed for write-off of weapons which has three members. We don't have to go into detail here. Then on the following page, we see in heading 3 what the methods and procedures are of the write-off of weapons. And in item 2, it is specified how to separate working from faulty parts in order to follow the procedure correctly. You're familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And it's something that was applied regularly in the weapons write-off procedure at the anti-terrorist unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. This was the only way that the inspection and write-off of weapons could be conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1202, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1202 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document 52222.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We're looking at a document signed by Mr. Markac, special minister's advisor, where you are ordered, as well as Mr. Bole, the chief of logistics, based on the inspection carried out on your unit, it's a request for 40 weapons to be serviced and then to proceed and issue the appropriate decision on write-off. Mr. Turkalj, we can see on page 2 a list of the weapons that are supposed to be inspected and evaluated, if it is possible to repair them or not, and the serial numbers of these weapons are provided, and we can note that it is not said which piece of weaponry was issued to which member of the unit. So it is an anonymous list, isn't it? You would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This order that we are looking at, was it something that would indicate anything extraordinary or unusual, deviating from the regular procedure in your experience?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No, it's nothing unusual. It's a list of weapons and the serial numbers, the type of weapon and the number, which was issued to the Lucko Anti-Terrorist Unit regardless of whether it was issued to the depot or to individual members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can we have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is P578.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Prashanthi, I obviously missed this. [Interpretation] Can we now look at 6170, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And now we will see another document on the same topic consisting of authorised persons or -- meant for the authorised persons at the anti-terrorist unit Lucko, and it says that based on the plan for the supervision and technical inspection of weapons on order of the special advisor to the minister, Mladen Markac. On 10th of November 1999, an inspection was carried out in the Lucko Anti-Terrorist Unit, and it was found that a number of weapons were malfunctioning and needed to be serviced or repaired. And then there is a list of weaponry that would be subject to inspection. So this is the list of weapons which was included in the previous order, the P578 that we looked at earlier. In this document, what is being described is the extent and the state of weapons pieces, what the malfunctions are, and it's an order of the special advisor to the minister, Mr. Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. This is the plan of the maintenance and technical inspection, and this is the plan that the inspection would be carried out after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D1203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1203 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this type of document can be found in the 65 examples to 2809, 2651, as well as 6167. I presume these documents are on the bar table list of the Prosecution, and therefore I won't press this topic any further. I just wanted to indicate that the documents refer to the same subject, the same topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As we saw the decision on what to do with weapons always needed to be made by the especially appointed commission. Isn't that correct, Mr. Turkalj?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the existence of such procedure points to the fact that inside the Ministry of the Interior, including, of course, the sector of special police, care was taken of weapons, and there were no independent voluntary decisions of individuals even if those included commanders to decide on the fate of weapons themselves?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Weapons and their use and handling is exclusively prescribed by the instructions of the Ministry of Interior. It was impossible to deal with equipment and weapons of this type in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: A few additional questions on the topic, Mr. Turkalj, before we break. During your examination-in-chief there was discussion about why the weapons of members of the anti-terrorist unit Lucko who took part in the search operation on the 25th of August in Grubori; that is, the 25th of August, 1995, was not exempt from the standard procedure. My question is the following: Does anyone, apart from the competent prosecutor, have a possibility to order that certain pieces of weaponry or objects be exempt and kept separately as evidence, or could that be done by the police themselves?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The police could not do that alone, since there were special instructions pertaining to equipment and weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason that particular care would be taken as regards the weapons of the special police unit of Lucko? Particularly in view of the fact that there was no evidence, no proof of which piece was issued to which particular member of the unit, when -- during -- when participating in an operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As regards the weapons inside the unit, the regular procedure was followed in terms of data on the weapons and the storing of the weapons as well as the details we have already discussed regarding servicing and maintenance of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us look at an exhibit. It is P625.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ERN number is 0465-1852.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is it a list of personnel of the anti-terrorist unit Lucko, who, on the 25th of August - it seems that the year is wrong. It should be 1995 instead of 2004 - took part in the military police operation Storm encirclement. We won't into any details on the list, but just to remind ourselves, we can see that each member of staff was issued with several different pieces of weaponry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that when participating in the operation, the particular staff member had to decide which of the weapons he had been issued with would -- he would take with him?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Out of the list of weapons they had been issued with, each particular staff member was free to choose the particular piece he deemed best for any particular operation or action, as regards the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Therefore, it depended solely on the type of operation.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Precisely so. And they would then take appropriate pieces with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we please look at 2852 next. 2852.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is a letter by Mr. Celic following a request of the police director, in which he states, in paragraph 2 that: "Considering that the anti-terrorist unit of Lucko does not have a record that would allow us to accurately determine what weapons the members of the Lucko Unit were using on the 25th of August, 1995 ..." Mr. Turkalj, does this assertion tally with your recollection and experience, that there was no separate record kept on who used what piece during the operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This is correct. It cannot be ascertained, since each staff member had a number of weapons that they had been issued with, and they decided themselves which weapon they would take for what operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, I would kindly ask a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think my bar table submission will be reduced, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D1204.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1204 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think it's an appropriate time for having a break, Your Honour, if you wish so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then have a break, and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before Mr. Turkalj -- I'd ask that he leave his headphones off for this. I just want to make the Court aware we did get the transcript reference with regard to my objection. Nowhere in the transcript reference that I received that I looked at with reference to what Mr. Celic said does it say that Mr. Celic told Drljo that Markac -- Mr. Celic said that he had heard Drljo tell Markac that he had burned houses. That is what I was objecting to before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was checking that. I have not found the references yet. But if we are talking about -- I was looking at page 40 of tape 2 of two side A.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. It's tape 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tape 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is -- if it's convenient on the e- court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll look at it later because I was also -- well, not to say worried about it, but that was the focus of my verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Just so --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I just say, I can say it with a sense of responsibility that not only in the statements of Mr. Celic but even in court, I read back what he had referred to with regard to the conversation between Markac and Drljo on the 26th. The argument, and, in fact, I have questioned him on this in court. So the objection was without merit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we have two issues now, whether it was put to Mr. Celic as a witness, that's one; and the second is whether what you said reflects what is Mr. Celic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I just want to be very very specific about this. The statement that was put to Mr. Turkalj was that Celic said that Drljo told Markac that he had burned houses. That's not what Celic said in the transcript life. That's not what Celic said in any conversation in an interview. And why is that important? Because that question is being put to Mr. Turkalj, who is basically the third level -- it's third level hearsay being put to him. Because Celic is overhearing Drljo talk to Markac. That's double hearsay in and of itself. Then that question is being put to Mr. Turkalj who said -- who talked to Celic. That is fourth level hearsay. So my problem with that is I don't disagree there was some discussion between Celic -- that Celic overheard that Drljo and Markac had no specific issues either in the trial transcript or in the interview were made about Drljo telling Markac himself that Drljo had burned houses and that really is very important obviously for obvious reasons, and that is why I objected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we shouldn't use time in court at this very moment to verify all of this. We are now hearing the evidence of Mr. Turkalj in cross-examination and nevertheless, of course, it's important for the Chamber to verify it, and we'll certainly do that but not at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkalj, just one more question in relation to the Grubori incident. I'm referring to your statement from 2004, which is P1149, paragraph 48. In this courtroom, on several occasions, there was mention of the fact which, to tell you the truth, was not corroborated by expert opinion, and that is that one of those killed in the Grubori incident had a cut throat. In your statement, paragraph 48, you said that when you were in Grubori and when you saw a male corpse that you thought you saw a gunshot wound to the body but that you were not certain. And you also stated that afterwards you heard that a knife wound was present on the body. First of all, who did you hear that piece of information from, that on the corpse that you had seen and on which you believed there was a gunshot wound that, in fact, it was a knife wound. Can you recall that now?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it is true what you said. As for the knife wound, if I recollect correctly, the investigator mentioned it to me. Prior to that, I had no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move to another topic, which is the topic of Storm and the use of artillery in the course of the operation. To start with, Mr. Turkalj, can you tell us precisely what your role was in Operation Storm? You were commander of the anti-terrorist unit Lucko, as you have said, but you had completed Military Academy and specialized in artillery; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your role in Operation Storm, regarding the use of the special forces of the Ministry of Interior had to do with artillery, correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. Solely with artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us look at document D543 together. This exhibit is something that the Chamber has already seen. It is an order by the chief of the Main Staff, General Cervenko, on the use of the special MUP forces during Operation Storm. Let us have a look at item 2 of the order, towards the bottom of the page. Thank you. Whereby it is stated that as regards the MUP special forces, the operation shall be carried out in two phases. In the first phase tactical surprise needs to be achieved by committing forces of adequate strength with considerable artillery support in order to reach the assigned locations. General Cervenko is referring to the use of the artillery of the special police forces. Can you tell us what sort of artillery of their own did the special police have that they could use in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As regards their own artillery, they had mixed artillery batteries comprising of a 120-millimetre mortars and 128-millimetres RAK 12 rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If we are to discuss the range of artillery, this Chamber has heard an expert witness who said that different types of artillery are used for different targets. If we try to define the type of artillery at the disposal of the special police, how would you categorise it, short-range or long-range artillery, and what is its use?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I would say it is short-range artillery. The mortars had the range of 6.200 metres; and RAK 12, 8.500 metres. It is short-range artillery mainly used to attack the front lines of the enemy and immediately behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the first phase when the special police artillery was used, we see that it includes the locations of Sveti Rok, Balonje [phoen], Vukova Kosa, and so on and so forth. It is the area of Mount Velebit. Can you tell us what is the lie of the land there and whether it is populated, whether the area is populated.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As regards the terrain there, it is mountainous, over 1.000 metres in altitude. In that area, there were no settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us move to the next page of the order, please, where General Cervenko mentions the second phase of the operation, in which he orders that the radio relay facility at Celavac needs to be taken control of as well as the tunnel at Prezid in order to join the 9th Guards Brigade forces. What is the importance of the Celavac facility?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Celovac facility was a communication centre used by the enemy. It dominated the entire communications network in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What about the pass and tunnel at Prezid?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The pass and at tunnel was along the road between Gracac and Obrovac, and we had to be able to control the road in order to prevent any link up of any enemy forces or introduction of new, fresh forces by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Registrar to kindly put up 65 ter 1893 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We just saw the order sent by the chief of Main Staff to the special police forces. In order to coordinate with the right-hand side neighbour which was the Military District Split as the Chamber has heard, the same order was sent to OG North, to Staff Brigadier Rahim Ademi personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us go to next page of this order in Croatian, towards the bottom of the page in Croatian. Let us go to the bottom of page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As you can see, Mr. Turkalj, there is an note, a remark here, beginning with the words: Brigadier, sir. And when we move on to page 3 we will see that the remark was drafted by Brigadier Rajko Rakic. It is a comment on Mr. Ademi's behalf of General Cervenko order. In item 2 he says that the launching of the MUP special forces operation will probably result in the Chetniks attacking the Pontoon bridge and other facilities and that it is necessary, therefore, to reinforce the area with artillery. The special police in the course of the first phase did receive reinforcements in terms of artillery by the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes. An artillery group was deployed to the foot of the Velebit mount.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will be dealing with that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we first have a number assigned to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1205, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit D1205 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the issue of these reinforcements, can the registrar call up P614, and can we turn to page 23 of the document, ERN number 0349-3618.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, this document is already in evidence. It is an analysis of the course of Operation Storm sent by the special police personally to the chief of the Main Staff, General Zvonimir Cervenko. Let's look at the page we have on our screens. This is part of the analysis referring to the rocket and artillery support of the joint forces of the special police in Operation Storm. Can we please have your comments on the rocket artillery support described herein? Look at the start of the text, where it is stated that the forces of the special police were provided support by, and there follows a list of weapons. Can you explain what this is it about.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This is my comment. The rocket artillery support for the special police was provided by six mortar batteries of 120 millimetres in calibre; one rocket battalion of RAKs, and they were along the same axis of attack; three 130-millimetre cannons; one 22-milimetres Grada multiple rocket launcher; and ten 107-millimetre light LRLs, and they were the ones used along the axis of attack of the special police during Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Please focus on 130-millimetre cannons. Were the weapons of the special police, or were they attached from the Croatian army as support along the axis of attack?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: They were attached to the special police along its axis of attack and were not part of the arsenal of the weapons of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The document goes on to detail the weapons used along the axis of attack. Their Honours are already aware of the fact that the special police advanced along one main axis and four auxiliary axes. Each of these axes had its own rocket artillery support. Can you describe for us in what way the artillery of the special police was used. Who called for that support, and who provided clearance for the use of artillery? What was the procedure like?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The procedure was very simple. Every axis of attack, including the main and auxiliary ones, had a rocket artillery battery designated for their purposes. Every commander of every axis referred to their own battery that they had assigned to them as their support and asked for the type of support that they needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, it is stated that the organisation of rocket and artillery support for the special police was reinforced by the rocket and artillery forces of the Croatian army. The document goes on to list them as the reinforced 130-millimetre cannon platoons and reinforced 122, D30 Howitzer platoons. First of all, can we agree that this is this long-rage artillery?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Well, this could be termed as medium to long-range artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page, page 24, we will see an entry which reads: "In addition to the rocket and artillery support provided to the joint forces of the police, the aforementioned long range artillery support provided support to the unit of the right hand neighbour." Mr. Turkalj, is this consistent with what you remember, that the artillery provided by the HV to the special police, in fact, provided support to both the special police forces and the HV, where these are the so-called termites; that's how the members of the unit were referred to?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This particular artillery group was intended for providing support to the forces of the special police and the HV, which also launched an attack at the foot of the Velebit mount, as well as to the HV forces that were attacking along the right-hand side of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this particular unit which provided support to the special police units did so at the request of yourself, or other members of the special police, and I'm referring to the commanders of individual axis, who referred to you, and that, in fact, it was not resubordinated to the units of the special police in the strict sense of the word?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: At the commencement of Operation Storm, the artillery group we're referring to provided support at the request of the special police, or, rather, through me. I was the one who designated the target that had to be engaged where necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I forgot one thing, Mr. Turkalj, when we were referring to 130-millimetre cannons a moment ago, we realized that the analysis mentioned them twice on the same page. Were these one and the same cannons that were used by the HV and which provided support for the special police units? You did say that the special police did not have that sort of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: These were the only cannons present in the area. There were none other than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that you sought support that was supposed to engage the previously designated targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the registrar please call up D549.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As for these targets, in the course of the -- this case we were able to see the internal control department which provided the command of the special police with intelligence concerning the extent of the enemy forces and the activities that are to be expected from the other side. Is it true that the information provided by the inner control department for the purposes of Operation Storm was, in fact, the basis upon which the targets engaged with artillery were designated?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: That's correct. The inner control department gathered intelligence in cooperation with the Croatian army and delivered the intelligence to me and probably to others.
